Michael — thanks for the note and the redline. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Naomi (procurement) to align on acceptable compromise language.

Quick context from our side: Redwood's standard is Delaware law for commercial contracts because it provides predictability for our larger enterprise agreements. That said, we're often able to accept alternative governing law in mid-market procurements if we can preserve a mechanism to get injunctive relief quickly (i.e., a court carveout for interim measures while arbitration proceeds).

Karthik / Naomi — can you review Acme's edits and see whether the following proposal is workable?

- Choice-of-law: New York state law (commercial contracts); but parties may elect Delaware for matters related to IP enforcement.
- Emergency relief: Arbitration will govern disputes, except that either party may seek temporary, injunctive or other emergency relief in state or federal court to preserve rights or evidence. Such relief shall not constitute a waiver of arbitration for the underlying dispute.

If legal signs off, we'll update the redline and send back. Naomi, please flag any procurement constraints on forum selection or service-of-process (Acme is US-based).

Thanks,
Irene

Michael / Irene / Naomi — legal here. Thanks for the helpful callout, Michael. My preliminary take: the compromise Irene proposed is reasonable for a deal of this size and keeps our ability to obtain rapid interim relief. Suggested edits below (I attached a short plain-text proposal as redwood_govlaw_proposal.txt).

Proposed contract language (draft):
- Governing Law: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflicts of law principles, except that matters concerning the validity or enforceability of Redwood's intellectual property shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
- Dispute Resolution; Interim Relief: Except as set forth below, any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved by final and binding arbitration conducted in accordance with the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in a court of competent jurisdiction (state or federal) to preserve the status quo, protect trade secrets, enforce confidentiality obligations, or prevent irreparable harm, and such right to seek interim relief shall not be deemed a waiver of any party's right to arbitrate the underlying dispute. Service of process for any such court proceeding may be effected in any manner permitted by law, including in the party's principal place of business.

Comments/risks:
- This preserves arbitration as the exclusive forum for final relief while allowing emergency court access (common carveout).
- We call out IP matters to keep Delaware law for a narrow set of issues; that reduces precedent risk for IP enforcement.
- Naomi: the service-of-process sentence is intentionally general; if Acme requires a specific agent or jurisdiction for service, we can add one, but that can create friction.

Next steps: if Acme accepts the draft text, we will incorporate it into a redline and circulate for final procurement signoff. I've attached the plain-text snippet for easy copy/paste.

—Karthik

Karthik / Irene — thanks, that language looks solid. A couple of quick points from Acme procurement:

- Acme is comfortable with the New York / Delaware split for IP.
- For service of process, procurement would prefer the clause to explicitly allow service in NY or CA (we're headquartered in NJ but have operations everywhere). If Redwood prefers to avoid specific locales, we can accept the current wording.
- On interim relief: procurement asked us to confirm that seeking emergency relief in court will not delay arbitration timelines or affect fees — we said no, it should be limited to preservation and won't change arbitration forum or fees.

If you can update the redline with the accepted text and add a short note on service-of-process (NY/CA allowed), we can close commercial terms and move to signature.

Happy to have procurement sign once updated.

Best,
Michael
